values.gym.cDrift: Drifting off maintenance — keep meal times and portions consistent.
values.gym.cFewData: Only one weigh-in — a single reading is noise. Aim for 2–3 next week.
values.gym.cFlat: Same weight as your last log — the trend needs a few more weigh-ins to grade.
values.gym.cGainFast: Gaining a bit fast — trim the surplus slightly so it's muscle, not fat.
values.gym.cNoData: No weigh-ins this week — the scale can't coach what it can't see. Log your weight.
values.gym.cOnPace: Right on track — keep doing exactly what you're doing.
values.gym.cStalled: Weight hasn't moved — tighten portions for one week, then re-check.
values.gym.cTooFast: Dropping too fast — add ≈200 kcal/day or you'll lose muscle, not just fat.
values.gym.cWaist: No waist logged — the tape shows fat loss even when the scale stalls.
values.gym.cWrongWay: Moving away from your goal — review the meal plan and daily steps.
values.gym.creatineT: The most-studied sports supplement in the world. 3–5g per day can modestly increase strength and power over weeks of training. Timing doesn't matter much — daily consistency does. It pulls water into muscles, so the scale may rise 1–2 kg at first (that's water, not fat). It is not a steroid. Drink plenty of water, skip the loading phase, and talk to a doctor first if you have kidney issues.
values.gym.draftHint: Type on the right — watch your numbers come alive behind this panel.
values.gym.estNote: Estimates from standard formulas — your weigh-ins tune the truth.
values.gym.fd1: Overnight oats + whey — 80g oats, 1 scoop, milk
values.gym.genNote: Built on your device from your calorie + protein targets and diet. Portions are ≈ estimates — adjust to taste. Not AI: nothing leaves your phone.
values.gym.iBfT: Estimated with the US Navy tape method (neck, waist, height). Accurate within a few percent for most people — a DEXA scan is the gold standard.
values.gym.iBmiT: Body Mass Index — weight relative to height. A rough screening tool, not a verdict: muscular people can score 'overweight' while being lean.
values.gym.iBmrT: Basal Metabolic Rate — the calories your body burns at complete rest in 24 hours. Estimated with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, the most validated formula.
values.gym.iCalT: Your target adds a goal adjustment to TDEE: −500/day to lose about 0.5 kg per week, +300/day to gain lean muscle slowly. Formulas are estimates — your weekly weigh-ins are the truth. Adjust if the trend stalls.
values.gym.iProteinT: Sports-nutrition research lands at about 1.6–2.2 g of protein per kg of body weight daily for building or keeping muscle. Spread it across 3–5 meals.
values.gym.iTdeeT: Total Daily Energy Expenditure — BMR multiplied by your activity level. Roughly what you burn on a normal day.
values.gym.mGainB: Big overnight oats — oats, milk, whey, peanut butter, banana · ≈750 kcal · 40g protein
values.gym.mGainD: Chicken pasta — pasta, chicken, tomato sauce, parmesan · ≈850 kcal · 55g protein
values.gym.mGainE: Greek yogurt + granola + honey · ≈400 kcal · 25g protein
values.gym.mGainL: Beef + 1.5 cups rice + veggies · ≈800 kcal · 50g protein
values.gym.mLoseB: Greek yogurt bowl — yogurt, berries, 1 tbsp honey · ≈320 kcal · 28g protein
values.gym.mLoseD: Baked white fish + broccoli + ½ cup rice · ≈480 kcal · 38g protein
values.gym.mLoseL: Grilled chicken salad — chicken breast, greens, olive oil + lemon · ≈450 kcal · 40g protein
values.gym.mMaintainB: Oatmeal + peanut butter + banana · ≈520 kcal · 18g protein
values.gym.mMaintainD: Salmon + sweet potato + greens · ≈620 kcal · 40g protein
values.gym.mMaintainL: Chicken rice bowl — chicken, 1 cup rice, veggies · ≈650 kcal · 45g protein
values.gym.mMaintainP: Apple + handful of almonds · ≈220 kcal · 6g protein
values.gym.mealsSub: ≈ means estimated. Hit your protein target first — calories second.
values.gym.measOpt: Body measurements — optional, for body-fat estimate
values.gym.noData: Log 2+ weeks to see your trend
values.gym.noDataHint: Weigh yourself weekly, same time of day, and log it here.
values.gym.r1i: 80g oats, 250ml milk, 1 scoop whey, 1 tbsp peanut butter, ½ banana, sliced
values.gym.r1s: 1. Mix everything except banana in a jar. 2. Refrigerate overnight. 3. Top with banana in the morning.
values.gym.r2i: 150g chicken breast, 1 cup cooked rice, mixed vegetables, 1 tbsp soy sauce, garlic
values.gym.r2s: 1. Season chicken with salt, pepper, garlic. 2. Pan-sear 6–7 min per side until cooked through. 3. Slice over rice and veggies, splash soy sauce.
values.gym.r3i: 1 cup red lentils, 1 onion, 1 tomato, turmeric, cumin, 1 cup rice
values.gym.r3s: 1. Sauté onion, add tomato and spices. 2. Add lentils + 3 cups water, simmer 20 min. 3. Serve over rice.
values.gym.r4i: 150g grilled chicken, mixed greens, ½ cucumber, 1 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice
values.gym.r4s: 1. Chop everything into a bowl. 2. Whisk oil + lemon + salt as dressing. 3. Toss and eat fresh.
values.gym.resetC: This clears your measurements, plan and progress. Nothing leaves your phone.
values.gym.setupSub: Tell us about your body and goal. We'll calculate your calories, macros and fuel plan — all estimates, tuned by your weekly weigh-ins.
values.gym.su_betaalaninet: ≈3.2 g daily. Helps you squeeze out extra reps on hard sets. Harmless skin tingling is normal.
values.gym.su_caffeinet: 3–6 mg per kg body weight, 30–60 min pre-workout. Sharper focus, better endurance. Skip it late in the day or it will steal your sleep.
values.gym.su_citrullinet: 6–8 g pre-workout. Boosts blood flow for a better pump. Moderate evidence.
values.gym.su_collagent: 10–15 g daily with vitamin C. Modest trial support for skin elasticity and hydration. Also kind to joints.
values.gym.su_hyalt: 120–200 mg daily. Modest evidence for skin hydration from within. Honest note: many studies are industry-funded.
values.gym.su_magt: 200–400 mg in the evening. Supports muscle function and sleep quality. Many diets run low.
values.gym.su_omega3t: 1–2 g EPA+DHA daily from fish oil or algae. General health support; modest direct muscle evidence.
values.gym.su_vitct: 75–200 mg daily. Your body needs it to build collagen; a strong antioxidant. Citrus and amla beat pills.
values.gym.su_vitdt: 1000–2000 IU daily if you get little sun. Supports muscle, bone and immunity. A blood test is the honest way to know your level.
values.gym.su_zinct: 8–11 mg daily. Immunity, recovery and skin repair. Do not mega-dose — excess zinc blocks copper absorption.
values.gym.suppNote: Supplements are the last 5%. Training, food and sleep do the rest. This isn't medical advice — check with a coach or doctor before starting anything.
values.gym.tipBulk: Slow the surplus slightly if the gain is mostly fat — check the mirror and waist.
values.gym.tipCut: You're still in a cut — keep protein high to protect muscle.
values.gym.tipHold: Maintenance is a win — keep training hard.
values.gym.tipWaist: Log your waist too, so you can see fat change even when weight stalls.
values.gym.tipWeigh: Weigh in at least once a week — trends beat single readings.
values.gym.title: Gym Fuel
values.gym.wheyT: Simply convenient protein — about 25g per scoop. It doesn't build muscle by itself; training + total daily protein does. Useful after workouts or when you can't cook. If milk bothers you, try isolate. Watch for added sugars in flavored powders. Food first, powder second.

values.askg.rate.d: Give your professor stars and a written review.
values.askg.rate.q: How do I rate a professor?
values.askg.rate.s1: Open the Home tab and tap Professors.
values.askg.rate.s2: Search your professor's name, or pick your campus to browse.
values.askg.rate.s3: Tap a professor, then tap Rate to open the rating sheet.
values.askg.rate.s4: Pick your stars and write a review — your name stays hidden and it posts as Anonymous.
values.askg.rate.s5: Keep it clean: no cursing or bad words. Comments are scanned automatically, and 3 blocked posts ban rating for a month.
values.askg.addprof.d: Can't find your professor? Create their profile.
values.askg.addprof.q: How do I add a professor that is missing?
values.askg.addprof.s1: Open the Home tab and tap Professors.
values.askg.addprof.s2: Search the name — if nothing matches, you'll see a note with an Add professor button.
values.askg.addprof.s3: Tap Add professor and fill in the name, campus, and department.
values.askg.addprof.s4: They appear in the list right away, ready to be rated.
values.askg.groups.d: Find and join communities near you.
values.askg.groups.q: How do I join a group?
values.askg.groups.s2: Browse Groups near you (50-mile radius) or search by name.
values.askg.groups.s3: Tap a group and hit Request to join.
values.askg.groups.s4: Once the admin approves, you can chat and call from the group page.
values.askg.chat.d: Text, pictures, GIFs and memes with your group.
values.askg.chat.q: How do I chat in a group?
values.askg.chat.s1: Open the Groups tab and tap your group.
values.askg.chat.s2: Tap the chat to open the conversation thread.
values.askg.chat.s3: Type a message — or open the sticker tab for Onaro's original GIF and meme pack.
values.askg.chat.s4: You can also share pictures and files up to 2 MB, plus links.
values.askg.calls.d: WhatsApp-style voice calls inside any group.
values.askg.calls.q: How do I start a group call?
values.askg.calls.s1: Open the Groups tab and tap your group.
values.askg.calls.s2: Tap the call button to start a group call — anyone in the group can join.
values.askg.calls.s3: Admins (and sub-admins) can mute people by tapping their tile; Mute all silences everyone but the admin.
values.askg.calls.s4: The speaking person's tile glows, so you can see who's talking at a glance.
values.askg.market.d: Buy and sell with people near you.
values.askg.market.q: How do I sell something on the marketplace?
values.askg.market.s2: Tap the post/sell button to create a listing.
values.askg.market.s3: Add photos, a price, and the details.
values.askg.market.s4: To buy, browse or search listings and message the seller from the listing.
values.askg.gym.d: Calories, macros, meal plans and body stats.
values.askg.gym.s1: Open the Daily tab and tap Gym Fuel.
values.askg.gym.s2: Do the one-time setup: sex, age, height, weight, activity level, and your goal.
values.askg.gym.s3: You get a live calorie ring, macro bars, BMI and body-fat estimates, plus day meal plans.
values.askg.gym.s4: Log your weight weekly to see your trend and weeks-to-goal estimate.
values.askg.calc.s1: Open the Daily tab and tap Calculator.
values.askg.calc.s2: Type like a real calculator — scientific keys are built in.
values.askg.calc.s3: Switch to the graph view to plot functions.
values.askg.calc.s4: Toggle DEG/RAD in the header for trigonometry.
values.askg.gpa.q: How do I calculate my GPA?
values.askg.gpa.s1: Open the Home tab and find the Grade Calculator card.
values.askg.gpa.s2: Tap add and enter a subject with its credit hours (0.5–12).
values.askg.gpa.s3: Pick the grade — A is 4 points, F is 0.
values.askg.gpa.s4: Your GPA updates live as you add subjects.
values.askg.capsule.d: Encrypted letters to your future self.
values.askg.capsule.q: How do I make a time capsule?
values.askg.capsule.s1: Open the Daily tab and tap Time Capsule.
values.askg.capsule.s2: Write a letter to your future self.
values.askg.capsule.s3: Pick an unlock date and seal it — it's encrypted on this device, and even you can't open it early.
values.askg.capsule.s4: It unlocks automatically when you open the app on or after that date.
values.askg.badges.d: Earn NEW, SILVER, GOLD, LEGEND and SPECIALIST.
values.askg.badges.s1: Open the Me tab to see your badges.
values.askg.badges.s2: Open Onaro at least a minute each day — every day counts as one qualifying login day.
values.askg.badges.s3: Climb NEW → SILVER (90 days) → GOLD (180) → LEGEND (365).
values.askg.badges.s4: Write 100+ professor reviews to earn SPECIALIST too.
values.askg.verify.d: How accounts get verified on Onaro.
values.askg.verify.q: How do I verify my account?
values.askg.verify.s1: Every Onaro account must be verified — no exceptions.
values.askg.verify.s2: Sign up with your phone number (with country code) and your email.
values.askg.verify.s3: Verify with EITHER an email code OR an SMS code — one of the two is enough.
values.askg.verify.s4: Then log in with your number or your email.
values.askg.settings.s1: Open the Me tab and tap Settings.
values.askg.settings.s2: Change language (28 languages), switch dark/light theme, or pick your country.
values.askg.settings.s3: Manage notifications from the same place.
values.askg.settings.s4: In this preview everything stays on your device — nothing is uploaded.
values.askg.events.d: See what's happening near you — or host it.
values.askg.events.s1: Open the Daily tab and tap Happening.
values.askg.events.s3: Tap an event for the details.
values.askg.events.s4: Hosting something? Create your own event from the Daily tab.

values.wel.foodSub: Period-aware nutrition ideas for each phase of your cycle.
values.wel.foodNote: General wellness information, not medical advice.
values.wel.fMen1: Iron-rich foods: spinach, lentils, beans, lean red meat — iron helps replace what bleeding takes.
values.wel.fMen2: Pair iron with vitamin C (citrus, bell peppers, tomatoes) to help your body absorb it.
values.wel.fMen3: Warm, easy meals: soups, broths, lentil soup, khichdi.
values.wel.fMen4: Magnesium-rich foods: pumpkin seeds, nuts, a little dark chocolate — may ease cramps.
values.wel.fMen5: Comforting herbal teas: ginger or chamomile.
values.wel.lMen1: Excess caffeine and alcohol — they can worsen fatigue and cramps.
values.wel.lMen2: Very salty snacks — they can increase bloating.
values.wel.mMen1: Spinach-lentil soup with a squeeze of lemon.
values.wel.mMen2: Warm oatmeal with dates and nuts.
values.wel.mMen3: Ginger tea with khichdi or plain rice and dal.
values.wel.fFol1: Lean proteins: eggs, chicken, fish, tofu, legumes.
values.wel.fFol3: Healthy fats: avocado, olive oil, nuts.
values.wel.fFol4: Whole grains and fermented foods like yogurt.
values.wel.lFol1: Very sugary drinks — they spike and crash your energy.
values.wel.lFol2: Skipping meals — steady fuel keeps energy smooth.
values.wel.mFol2: Grilled chicken or fish with a big salad.
values.wel.fOvu1: Fiber-rich vegetables: broccoli, cauliflower, kale, cabbage.
values.wel.fOvu4: Plenty of water, plus hydrating foods like cucumber and watermelon.
values.wel.fOvu5: Eggs and lean protein to keep energy steady.
values.wel.mOvu3: Cucumber-mint water with a light protein bowl.
values.wel.fLut1: Complex carbs: sweet potato, brown rice, oats — steady energy for cravings.
values.wel.fLut2: Magnesium: a little dark chocolate, bananas, nuts, seeds.
values.wel.fLut4: Leafy greens plus protein at each meal.
values.wel.fLut5: Warm herbal tea in the evening.
values.wel.lLut1: Excess caffeine — it can disturb sleep and mood.
values.wel.lLut2: Very salty foods — they can worsen bloating.

values.wel.d1: Eat iron-rich foods on bleeding days, with vitamin C alongside.
values.wel.d2: Drink water through the day — warm fluids count too.
values.wel.d3: Eat regular meals; skipping can worsen fatigue and mood dips.
values.wel.d4: For cramps, many people find comfort in ginger tea, warm soups, and magnesium-rich foods.
values.wel.d5: For bloating, water and potassium-rich foods like bananas help; go easy on salt.
values.wel.d6: Limit excess caffeine, alcohol, and very salty foods during your period.
values.wel.hubSub: Short, practical guides for taking care of yourself.
values.wel.a1T: Caring for yourself during your period
values.wel.a11: Change pads, tampons, or cups every 4–8 hours — never wear protection far longer than recommended.
values.wel.a12: Shower or bathe daily; mild, unscented soap is enough. Bathing during your period is completely fine.
values.wel.a13: Wear breathable cotton underwear and change promptly if it feels damp.
values.wel.a14: Keep a small period kit for school or work: spare protection, wipes, and anything that comforts you.
values.wel.a15: Eat balanced meals and drink water through the day to steady your energy.
values.wel.a21: Heat helps: a warm water bottle or heating pad on your lower belly relaxes muscles.
values.wel.a22: Gentle movement — walking, stretching, light yoga — can ease pain over time.
values.wel.a23: Rest when you need it; needing extra sleep during your period is normal.
values.wel.a24: Warm drinks like ginger or chamomile tea can be soothing.
values.wel.a25: Slow deep breathing and relaxation can lower how intense pain feels.
values.wel.a26: If pain is severe, getting worse, or regularly stops you living normally, talk to a healthcare professional.
values.wel.a31: Mood dips before a period are common — be kind to yourself on low days.
values.wel.a32: Keep sleep regular; tiredness makes everything feel harder.
values.wel.a33: Magnesium and B6-rich foods (nuts, bananas, whole grains) help some people.
values.wel.a34: Small comforts count: gentle movement, journaling, music, time with people you trust.
values.wel.a35: If low mood feels overwhelming or doesn't lift, consider speaking with a qualified healthcare professional.
values.wel.a4T: Heavy or long periods — know the facts
values.wel.a41: Educational fact: a period lasting longer than 7 days is considered heavy bleeding.
values.wel.a42: Soaking through a pad or tampon every hour for several hours in a row is a sign to get checked.
values.wel.a43: Passing clots larger than a quarter, or needing to change protection at night, also count as heavy.
values.wel.a44: Common problems people report: fatigue, weakness, dizziness, shortness of breath — heavy bleeding can lower iron.
values.wel.a45: Self-care basics: track your flow, rest, eat iron-rich foods, and stay hydrated.
values.wel.a46: Seek care promptly for: soaking a pad/tampon an hour for 2+ hours in a row, bleeding between periods, or fainting with bleeding.
values.wel.a47: Treatments exist — heavy periods are not something you simply have to live with.
